items.e: AND MIRIAM…SPOKE. Miriam spoke. Aaron agreed or was silent. Hence he was also punished.

Va-tedabber (spoke) is followed by a bet and has a negative connotation. It is similar to va-yedabber ha-am be-Elohim (And the people spoke against God) (Num. 21:5). The verb dabber (spoke) followed by a bet is also found with a positive connotation. It also appears in prophetic statements. Some say that Moses was king of Cush and took a Cushite woman. Onkelos renders Cushite, beautiful. According to Onkelos, Cushite is an honorific term. The Arabs similarly call pitch white. We too refer to a blind person by the term sege nahor (rich of light). But it is illogical to turn a positive name into a negative one. Some say that Cush the Benjaminite (Ps. 7:1) refers to Saul. They say the same with regard to Are ye not as the children of the Ethiopians (Khushiyyim) unto Me (Amos 9:7). I have already explained this.I believe that the Cushite woman is to be identified with Zipporah, for Zipporah was a Midianite. The Midianites are Ishmaelites and they live in tents. Scripture similarly writes: The curtains of the land of Midian do tremble (Hab. 3:7). Because of the sun they do not have any whiteness at all. Zipporah was black and was like a Cushite.

[FOR HE HAD MARRIED A CUSHITE WOMAN.] These are the words that Miriam spoke. How precious are the words of the ancients who said with regard to the elders, “Happy are they, but woe to their wives.” They suspected that Moses refrained from sleeping with Zipporah only because she was not beautiful.

AND THEY SAID: HATH THE LORD INDEED SPOKEN ONLY WITH MOSES? Miriam offered proof that Moses did not act in this manner because of the sanctity of God, for they too were prophets and they were not prohibited from engaging in sexual intercourse.
ONLY WITH. Scripture reads, ha-rak akh . One term would have sufficed. However, Scripture is employing elegant language. Compare, ha-mi-mi-beli en kevarim (because there were no graves) (Ex. 14:11).
AND THE LORD HEARD IT. Even though they spoke in secret.
WAS VERY MEEK. The word anav (meek) is similar to the word shalev (at peace) (Job 16:12). Its meaning is that Moses did not seek honor over his brother.

SUDDENLY. The mem of pitom (suddenly) is superfluous. It is like the mem of shilshom (three days ago). Pitom is related to peti (a thoughtless one) (Prov. 9:4). It refers to something that one did not think of.

COME OUT YE THREE UNTO THE TENT OF MEETING. Each one from his tent. Scripture first speaks generally. It then goes into detail, namely, And the Lord came down in a pillar of cloud…and called Aaron and Miriam (v. 5), and Moses heard.
HEAR NOW MY WORDS. The word na means now.
A PROPHET AMONG YOU. If there be a prophet of God among you.

IN A VISION The meaning of im yiheyeh nevi’akhem Adonai (if there be a prophet among you, I the Lord) is, if there be a prophet, one who is a prophet of God among you. Compare, ve-hanevu’ah oded ha-navi (even the prophecy of Oded the prophet (II Chron. 15:8); and ha-ohelah sarah immo (his mother Sarah’s tent) (Gen. 24:67); and kisakha Elohim olam (Thy throne given of God is for ever) (Ps. 45:7).
IN A VISION. In the visions of the night.
I DO SPEAK WITH HIM IN A DREAM. Scripture repeats itself as is its style in prophecies.

HE IS TRUSTED IN ALL MY HOUSE. It means that Moses is, at it were, a member of My house. He enters without permission. If necessary he states his needs. However, in your case when I make myself known to you in a dream, then you are informed. If not, then you have no permission to ask.
WITH HIM DO I SPEAK MOUTH TO MOUTH. The meaning is, I speak to him without an intermediary.
EVEN MANIFESTLY, AND NOT IN DARK SPEECHES. This means I illustrate my word to him as I did when I commanded the erection of the tabernacle.
AND NOT IN DARK SPEECHES. Compare, A great eagle ( …Came unto Lebanon, And took the top of the cedar ) (Ezek. 17:3).
AND THE SIMILITUDE OF THE LORD DOTH HE BEHOLD. As in the case of Show me, I pray Thee, Thy glory (Ex. 33:18). Or its meaning is that God communicates with Moses when Moses is awake.
AND HE DEPARTED. The reference is to God’s glory. And when the cloud was removed (v. 10) proves this.
FROM OVER THE TENT. From over the opening of the tent.
AND…BEHOLD, MIRIAM WAS LEPROUS. Ve-hinneh metzora’at is to be rendered, and behold, “she” [Miriam] was leprous. Compare, ka’asher ka’ah (as it vomited out) (Lev. 18:28).
OH MY LORD. I have already explained the meaning of bi adoni (Oh my lord).
LAY NOT, I PRAY THEE. The meaning of al na (…not, I pray thee) is, now, do not.

WE HAVE DONE FOOLISHLY. The word no’alnu (we have done foolishly) is a nifal . It has no cognate except for the word no’alu (are become fools) in The princes of Zoan are become fools (Is. 19:13). Some say that the root of no’alnu was formed by inverting the root ivvelet (foolishness). Compare, Foolishness is bound up (Prov. 22:15) (in the heart of a child). The meaning of no’alnu is known.

LET HER NOT, I PRAY, BE AS ONE DEAD. Let our sister not now be as a stillborn child, half of whose flesh is consumed when it comes out of its mother’s womb. The same is true of the flesh of a leper. There is no need for a scribal emendation.
AND MOSES CRIED. This shows that Moses was pained because of what happened to his sister.

O GOD. You who hold the power in Your hands, heal her now. God therefore answered him as follows: If her father was angry at her and spat in her face, would she not hide in shame from seeing his face for seven days?
SHUT UP. As lepers are, so that they do not harm others.

AND AFTER THAT SHE SHALL BE BROUGHT IN AGAIN. Ve-acher te’asef (and after that she shall be brought in again) means she shall once again be considered as a member of the community. Va-asafto (and you shall bring him in) in and you shall bring him in from his leprosy (II Kings 5:3) is similar. After Miriam returned to the camp, the people journeyed from Hazeroth.

AND PITCHED IN THE WILDERNESS OF PARAN. Many believe that the cloud was there. They interpret thus because they found Scripture stating and the cloud abode in the wilderness of Paran (Num. 10:12). They interpret And when the cloud was removed from over the Tent (v. 10) literally. However, I believe that this is not the correct meaning.
SEND THOU MEN. Scripture records that God told Israel: go up, take possession (Deut. 1:21) and Israel answered: Let us send men before us (Deut. 1:22). God then said, Send thou men .
The meaning of men is, men known for their might. The same applies to all of them men (v. 3) and to be thou [Solomon] strong and show thyself a man (I Kings 2:2), for he [Solomon] was a man.
THAT THEY MAY SPY OUT. The meaning of ve-yaturu (that they may spy out) is that they may search out. Compare, ve-lo taturu (and that ye go not about) (Num. 15:39).

EVERY ONE A PRINCE AMONG THEM. Kol nasi ba-hem is to be interpreted: each one was a prince among them. On the other hand, the word ehad mentioned earlier in our verse also applies here. Compare, And two men, captains of bands, were [captains of] the son of Saul (II Sam. 4:2). There are many such examples.

[THESE ARE THE NAMES OF THE MEN.] The reason that Scripture states, these are the names of the men , after earlier stating, And these were their names (v. 4), is to teach us that, unlike Hoshea, their names were never changed.

GET YOU UP HERE INTO THE SOUTH. Get you up this way in the south. It is known that Egypt is south of the land of Israel, as I have explained in the Book of Daniel. The following is proof of this. Egypt is less than thirty degrees north of the equator. Jerusalem is thirty-three degrees north of the equator. The desert of Paran is south of the land of Canaan. Observe that the meaning of in the South is not south of the camp but in the south of the land of Canaan. Proof of the aforementioned is that Scripture tells us concerning Hebron, which belonged to the tribe of Judah, Judah shall abide in his border on the south (Josh. 18:5).
AND SEE THE LAND, WHAT IT IS. And the people, what is it?
WHETHER THEY ARE STRONG. In battle. Scripture then goes on to explain, and see the land . It says, and what the land is…whether it is good , that is, whether its air and water are good.
WHETHER IN CAMPS. Like the Kederites, who live in tents.
WHETHER IT IS FAT. In producing wheat.
[AND CAME UNTO HEBRON.] Our sages of blessed memory said that and came refers to Caleb the son of Jephunneh, for each one of the men went to a different part of the country.

ZOAN IN EGYPT. Zoan is the name of a city in Egypt. Of Beth-lehem Judah (Ruth 1:1) is similar. Some say that the word tzo’an (Zoan) is connected to the word yitzan (be removed) in A tent that shall not be removed (Is. 33:20). However, this is farfetched.
Scripture mentions Hebron in order to tell us that Hebron came into being before Zoan.
UNTO THE VALLEY OF ESHCOL. These are the words of Moses. It is possible that it is similar to and pursued as far as Dan (Gen. 14:14) in that it had another name.
WAS CALLED. Kara (was called) is to be rendered, someone called. Compare, whom she bore to Levi (Num. 26:59).

[AT THE END.] The word mi-ketz (at the end) sometimes means at the beginning and sometimes means at the end. Mi-ketz arba’im yom (and the end of forty days) probably means at the start of the fortieth day.
AND THEY WENT. This informs us that they did not go to their tents, which were in the camp, but immediately went [to Moses, Aaron, and all the congregation].
AND BROUGHT BACK WORD. To Moses and Aaron.
AND THEY TOLD HIM. They told Moses, for he was the most important one.
AND CALEB STILLED THE PEOPLE. Rabbi Jonah the grammarian says that the meaning of va-yahas (and…stilled) is: and he said be still ( hasu ).

AND THEY SPREAD AN EVIL REPORT OF THE LAND. Va-yotzi’u dibbat ha-aretz (and they spread an evil report) means: and they spread a lie. This is not the meaning of va-yave yosef et dibbatam ra (and Joseph brought evil report of them) (Gen. 37:2), for va-yave (brought) is the reverse of va-yotzi (and they spread).

EVIL REPORT. The word dibbah (evil report) comes from a double root. It comes from the same root as the word dovev (moving gently) in Moving gently the lips of those that are asleep (Cant. 7:10). I have explained it in its place.
EATETH UP THE INHABITANTS THEREOF. For its air is bad.

MEN OF GREAT STATURE. Every man is a man of measurements. Anshe middot means men of great measurement, men whose measurements are greater than everyone else’s. The same applies to the phrase anshe levav (men of heart) (Job. 34:34). There are many other instances similar to the above.
THE NEPHILIM. I have already explained this term.
OF THE NEPHILIM. Its meaning is that they were of the Nephilim, who were in the earth in those days, and also after that when…came in (Gen 6:4). I have explained it there.
THEIR VOICE. Et kolam (their voice) is the object of va-tissa (lifted up) and also of va-yittenu (and cried).
MURMURED. Va-yillonu (murmured) is a nifal . It is an ayin vav . When conjugated in the nifal it looks like a whole root.

TO RETURN INTO EGYPT. Shuv (to return) is an infinitive. It is like the word kum (to stand) in I am not able to stand (Lam. 1:14) and kum (rising up) in And the king, against whom there is no rising up (Prov. 30:31).
THEN MOSES…FELL. By his own will.
AND JOSHUA THE SON OF NUN. Moses mentions Joshua first out of regard for Joshua’s elevated status.
FOR THEY ARE BREAD. We will eat them like bread. Who eat up My people as they eat bread (Ps. 14:4) is similar.
THEIR DEFENSE IS REMOVED FROM OVER THEM. For the heart of a warrior frets when he does not have a shield to protect him and to serve as a shade for him.
BADE STONE THEM. Joshua and Caleb.
DESPISE ME. Yena’atzuni (despise me) means anger me. It has many cognates in Scripture.
Scripture employs the singular be-kirbo (among them) because at first they were united to do good.

WHEN THE EGYPTIANS SHALL HEAR–FOR THOU BROUGHTEST UP THIS PEOPLE. The meaning of ki he’elita (for thou broughtest up) is: that you brought up. After Scripture states, When the Egyptians shall hear (ve-shame’u)…they will say to the inhabitants of this land , the reference being to the land of Canaan, it goes on to explain what the Egyptians heard. Scripture therefore repeats the word shame’u (have heard) and states they have heard (shame’u) that Thou Lord [Thy glory] art in the midst of this people (v. 14).

ART SEEN FACE TO FACE. The reference is to the glory which the elders saw (Ex. 24:9,10), or to the appearance of the glory of the Lord…in the eyes of the children of Israel (Ex. 24:17). The latter is correct.

ART SEEN. The word nirah (seen) is a verb in the perfect. The meaning of attah Adonai nirah is, Thou Lord were seen. Ve-nishar ani (and I was left) (Ezek. 9: 8) is similar. So is ki umlal ani (for I languish away) (Ps. 6:3), because the lamed of umlal is vocalized with a pattach .
STANDETH OVER THEM. When they camp.
THEN THE NATIONS WHICH HAVE HEARD THE FAME OF THEE. The reference is to Egypt. Also to the Canaanites and other nations.
ABLE. The word yekholet (able) is a noun. It is similar to the word yevoshet (dried up) in until the waters were dried up (Gen. 8:7). It does not mean a measure as in the midrashic interpretation.
THEREFORE HE HATH SLAIN THEM IN THE WILDERNESS. The meaning of va-yishchatem is, He hath slain them. Scripture employs the term va-yishchatem because sheep graze in the wilderness.

LET THE POWER OF THE LORD BE GREAT. Let the power…be great connotes being slow to anger, for all who are long-suffering have the great power to break their anger. As Thou hast spoken , that you are slow to anger is proof of this. I have explained these attributes in the Torah portion Ki Tissa .

PARDON, I PRAY THEE. Since we find Scripture saying surely they shall not see the land (v. 23) after salachti ke-devarekha (I have pardoned according to thy word) (v. 20), we learn that the term salach (pardon) refers to being slow to anger. Similarly, the meaning of ve-nislach lo (and he shall be forgiven) (Num 15:28) is [the punishment shall be held in abeyance] until he fully repents.
ACCORDING UNTO THE GREATNESS OF THY LOVINGKINDNESS. The meaning of ke-godel chasdekha (according to the greatness of Thy lovingkindness) is: because of Thy great lovingkindness.
AND ACCORDING AS THOU HAST FORGIVEN. The word nasata (Thou hast forgiven) is similar to the word nose (forgiving) in forgiving sin (Ex. 34:7).

EVEN UNTIL NOW. Until this place or from the day that they left Egypt until this very day, for the word hennah (now) can refer to a place or to a specific time. Compare, there came men in hither (hennah) (Josh. 2:2) and, and I have not seen him until now (hennah) (Gen. 44:28). I have already explained this term.
AS I LIVE. It means as I live, so shall My word come to pass.
SHALL BE FILLED WITH THE GLORY. As My glory fills the earth. However, it most probably refers to the future. Its meaning is, I shall do this so that my glory shall be known in the world.

THESE TEN TIMES. The meaning is, these many times. Scripture mentions ten because it is most important. It is the end of the one numbers and the first of the ten numbers in the second series of numbers.
ANY OF THEM THAT DESPISED ME. From among their children.

BUT MY SERVANT CALEB. Caleb alone is mentioned because he stilled the people (Num. 13:30). The Levites and the kohanim are not included in the oath, for no prince from among them went to spy out the land. Furthermore, Scripture states, all that were numbered of you, according to your whole number (v. 29). Now even though there were no kohanim there, there were in reality many Levites there.
ANOTHER SPIRIT. In contrast to the spies.
AND HATH FOLLOWED ME FULLY. He did not he but pursued my word and confirmed it by saying that the land is very good.

NOW THE AMALEKITE AND THE CANAANITE. The Canaanite refers to the Amorite, for every Amorite is a Canaanite. Scripture does not bother to mention the Amorite by name because the other nation mentioned is the Amalekite, who is of the children of Shem. On the other hand, Canaan, who is the father of the Amorite, is of the children of Ham. Then the Amalekite and the Canaanite…came down (Num. 14:45) is similar. And the Amorites…came out (Deut. 1:44) is proof of this. Scripture does not mention the Amalekite in the aforementioned verse, as the Amorite was the more important.

DWELT IN THE VALE. To ambush you. Others say that the meaning of our verse is, even though the Amalekite and the Canaanite dwell in the valley, turn toward the way of the Red Sea and do not fear. Now the Israelites did not repent, hence God’s word.
YOUR CARCASSES. The meaning of pigrekhem is your dead bodies.
HAVE MURMURED. Halinotem (have murmured) is related to the word va-yallinu (murmured) in and…murmured against Moses (v. 2).
CONCERNING WHICH I LIFTED UP MY HAND. Scripture speaks as humans do, for the sky is above.
Caleb is mentioned first because he acted before anyone else to quiet the people.
YOUR CARCASSES. Namely, you.
SHALL BE WANDERERS. For it is the way of shepherds not to remain and rest in one place. My habitation is plucked up and carried away from me As a shepherd’s tent (Is. 38:12) is proof of this.
YOUR STRAYINGS. For you turned away from me and said, Let us make a captain, and let us return into Egypt (Num. 14:4).
WHICH YE SPIED OUT. By command.
MY DISPLEASURE. I will break my word. Or, it means who shall break Me; that is, who shall break My oath. Compare, But if her father break (heni) her (Num 30:6).
THAT ARE GATHERED TOGETHER AGAINST ME. For they wanted to stone the servants of God because they spoke of God’s glory.
IN THIS WILDERNESS. The time set for each one shall come to an end, for God has set a specific time for everyone’s death.
AND THERE THEY SHALL DIE. All of them, close to the time set by God.
And…MADE ALL THE CONGREGATION TO MURMUR AGAINST HIM. Va-yillonu (and made to murmur) is a hifil .
DIED. Va-yamutu (died) is to interpreted as if written metu (died).
BY THE PLAGUE. All together.
BUT JOSHUA THE SON OF NUN. These are the words of Moses. He mentions Joshua before Caleb.
SEEING IT SHALL NOT PROSPER. The ascent of the mountain will not prosper. Or, the violation of God’s command cannot prosper.
FORASMUCH AS YE ARE TURNED BACK. Ki al ken shavtem (forasmuch as ye are turned back) means, since you turned back. Compare, since (ki al ken) I gave her not (Gen. 38:26).
BUT THEY PRESUMED TO GO UP. Va-yapilu (but they presumed) is related to the word ofel (mound) in the mound and the tower (Is. 32:14). The meaning of va-yapilu is, they went up the hill.

AND BEAT THEM DOWN. Rabbi Moses the Spaniard, of blessed memory, says that our text should have read va-yakkitum (and beat them down). Va-yadbeku (followed hard) in even they also followed hard after them (I Sam. 14:22) is similar. However, I believe that va-yakketum (and beat them down) comes from a double root and is an irregular word.
EVEN UNTO HORMAH. Hormah is the name of a place. Others say that the meaning of even unto Hormah is, until they destroyed them.

WHEN YE ARE COME INTO THE LAND OF YOUR HABITATIONS. This chapter follows [the one dealing with the spies] in order to console the children by informing them that they would enter the land, for the Israelites grew weak and mourned. However, the real reason that this chapter follows the one dealing with the spies, is because all the congregation shouted and sinned. God forgave their sin because of the prayer of Moses. Scripture says, And when ye shall err (15:22). And they shall be forgiven (15:25) is proof of this. Scripture found it necessary to mention the law of the meal offering and of all burnt offerings and sacrifices. At the end, it states, But the soul that doeth aught with a high hand (v. 30). The latter alludes to Israel’s deeds. Scripture mentions the gatherer of wood (verses 32-34) because he acted with a high hand. God designated the fringes as a sign because of His great pity on Israel, so that a person will not act with a high hand or forget.

CLEARLY UTTERED. Le-fale (clearly uttered) means to separate. Similarly the word ve-hiflah (shall make a division) in And the Lord shall make a division (Ex. 9:4). This is so even though ve-hiflah is spelled with a heh , for the letters alef, heh, vav, yod interchange.9.
A MEAL-OFFERING OF…FINE FLOUR. A tenth of an ephah for each one of the flock.

THE HE-LAMBS. Or the kids. Scripture similarly states later, for each lamb . If the celebrant offers a ram, then his meal offering is doubled, for a lamb is a small animal. Scripture does not mention the free-will offering along with the bullock. It mentions the peace offering [with the bullock] because it did not mention it above. They all have one law.
[ACCORDING TO THE NUMBER.] The reference is to the meal offering, the oil, and the wine.
OR WHOSOEVER MAY BE AMONG YOU. Today.

AS FOR THE CONGREGATION. Some say that the heh prefixed to the word kahal (congregation) is the sign of the vocative. However, I believe that there is no vocative letter in the holy tongue. The four instances are proof of this. One of them is Moses, Moses . On the contrary, this heh is the sign of the definite object. It is not a sign of the vocative.
AS YE ARE, SO SHALL THE STRANGER BE. I have already explained the rule governing two kafs joined together.

[ONE LAW.] Its meaning is, one law aside from the burnt offerings, for the burnt offerings are obligated by statute. God also says, as you bring a meal offering of fine flour along with the burnt offering, thus shall you do with your dough. There is no need to mention what our ancients, of blessed memory, received by tradition, namely, that one is obligated to set aside two offerings, a portion of the dough and a portion of the grain, and their amount. Their words are true. Everything else is nonsense.

[ONE HE-GOAT.] Scripture adds a he-goat. The congregation must bring a sin offering whether they erred by doing something they were prohibited from doing or erred in not doing something they were obligated to do.

AND THEIR SIN-OFFERING. The reference is to the he-goat. A sei’r izzim (he-goat) refers to a young goat because the word se’ir (he-goat) is connected to izzim (goats). The reverse is the case with the term atud (he-goat).

A SHE-GOAT OF THE FIRST YEAR FOR A SIN-OFFERING. This explains a goat, a female (Lev. 4:28). The sin spoken of in our verse refers to a failure, due to error, to do what the Torah commands. Now this law is the same for the one who errs and does what he is commanded not to do.
ONE LAW. This is similar to This is the law of (torat) the sin-offering (Lev. 6:18).
WITH A HIGH HAND. To show all that he does not fear God.
BLASPHEMETH. This is the way people speak.
BECAUSE HE HATH DESPISED THE WORD OF THE LORD. This is what with a high hand refers to.
AND HATH BROKEN HIS COMMANDMENT. For God commanded him not to act with a high hand. Others say that and hath broken His commandment refers to one who violates God’s commandment in secret.
THAT SOUL. This does not refer to the rational soul. as those who err say. It refers rather to the connection of the soul to the body.
HIS INIQUITY SHALL BE UPON HIM. Compare, his blood shall be upon him (Ezek. 33:4).

IN THE WILDERNESS. I believe that the reference is to the wilderness of Sinai. I have already mentioned why this chapter follows the incident of the spies. It is also possible that the gatherer of wood acted with a high hand and they warned him, but to no avail.[33. BROUGHT HIM.] Some say they brought him in on Saturday night.
IN WARD. Ba-mishmar (in ward) is vocalized with a pattach . It refers to a specific place.
WHAT SHOULD BE DONE TO HIM. How he should be put to death.
AS THE LORD COMMANDED. Death by stoning.

THAT THEY MAKE THEM…FRINGES. It is possible to interpret this in two ways. One, that they make fringes ( tzitzit ) like those in by the fringes (be-tzitzit) of my head (Ezek. 8:3), the reference in our verse being to threads that are not woven.
IN THE CORNERS OF THEIR GARMENTS. Upon smooth garments or pants, for if pants are divided they will have corners.
A THREAD OF BLUE. Upon the fringes. The reason the thread was blue is that blue is a sky-like color.

AND IT SHALL BE UNTO YOU FOR A FRINGE. The thread at the end was like the fringe. The other interpretation is the one which the rabbis of blessed memory transmitted. Now the first interpretation is nullified in view of the fact that there are true witnesses to the second explanation. The rabbis transmitted to us the law that this commandment applies to a garment that has four corners and that the tzitzit are fringes. I will explain this law later. Now this commandment states that everyone who has a four-cornered garment shall always cover himself with it during the day. He shall not remove it so that he remembers the commandments. Those who pray with a tallit during the time of prayers do so because they read in the shema , And it shall be unto you for a fringe (v. 39) and that they make them throughout their generations fringes (v. 38). However, I believe that one is more obligated to enwrap oneself in fringes when he is not at prayer than during the time of prayer, so that he remembers the commandments and does not err and trespass during the other hours of the day, for in the hour of prayer he will not sin.
THAT YE MAY LOOK UPON IT. The commandment requires that the fringes be seen.

AFTER YOUR OWN HEART. Which lusts. The eye sees and the heart desires. The fringes thus serve as a sign and a mark that a person should not pursue the thoughts of his heart and all that his eyes desire.
AFTER WHICH YE USE TO GO ASTRAY. For one who follows his desires goes astray from the service of his God.

THAT YE MAY REMEMBER. Scripture has previously stated, and remember all the commandments of the Lord (v. 39). The meaning of our verse is: if you remember the commandments of God, you will be holy and you will not defile yourselves with the lusts of the heart which defile the rational soul.
I AM THE LORD YOUR GOD. I am He who took you out of Egypt to be your God. I therefore say to you: I am the Lord your God .

NOW KORAH, THE SON OF IZHAR…TOOK. This event occurred in the wilderness of Sinai when the first-born were set aside and the Levites were placed in their stead. Israel thought that our master Moses acted out of his own will in giving his brother an elevated position. They suspected that he acted similarly towards the sons of Kohath, who were his relatives, and to all the sons of Levi who were of his family. The Levites rebelled against Moses because they were subservient to Aaron and his sons. Dathan and Abiram rebelled because Moses removed the birthright from Reuben their forefather, and gave it to Joseph. It is also possible that they suspected that Moses favored the tribe of Joseph because Joshua was his assistant. Korah too was a first-born, as Scripture clearly states. The banner of Reuben camped in the south. So did Korah, for he was a Kohathite. The princes of the congregation were first-born. They offered the burnt offering. They therefore took the fire pans. The miracle of the staff, which demonstrated to all of Israel that God chose the Levites in place of the first-born, is proof that this explanation is correct. Hence Scripture reads, that there may be made an end of their murmurings against Me (Num. 17:25), for the murmuring was an account of this. Moses also said, that I have not done them of mine own mind (v. 28). He said the aforementioned because Israel had come to believe that he had acted on his own. Furthermore, Moses said, then the Lord hath not sent me (v. 29) in this thing, because Israel had come to believe in him. Here is another rigorous proof: seeing all the congregation are holy (v. 3). The aforementioned alludes to the first-born who are holy, for Scripture states, Sanctify unto Me all the first-born (Ex. 13:2). The first-born were the priests that come near to the Lord (Ex. 19:22). They were the most important ones of the congregation.

NOW KORAH…TOOK. This is short for, now Korah took men. Compare, an ass bread (I Sam. 16:20). There are many such instances in Scripture. Rabbi Jonah says that the meaning of Now Korah took is now Korah took himself to rise against Moses.
IN THE FACE OF MOSES. They did not rise up in secret. There is a difference between li-fene (in the face of) and mi-pene (before the face of) (Gen. 3:8).
THE ELECT MEN OF THE ASSEMBLY. They were called to the tent of meeting.

MEN OF RENOWN. Before they left Egypt.A grammarian says that the princes of the congregation are the leaders who stood over those that were numbered (Num 1:4). He says that they are the object of took. Our text should be read as if written, And Korah and Dathan and Abiram and On took the princes of Israel to speak to them. This interpretation is a bit far-fetched.
YE TAKE TOO MUCH UPON YOU. Enough for you. Its meaning is, you have grabbed the greater portion.
SEEING ALL THE CONGREGATION ARE HOLY. For the entire congregation became holy from the day they stood on Sinai.

AND THE LORD IS AMONG THEM. For the Levites were chosen after God’s glory dwelt amidst the children of Israel. Now if Moses knew when he was on Mount Sinai that the tribe of Levi was chosen, Israel did not know.
WHEREFORE THEN LIFT YE UP YOURSELVES ABOVE THE ASSEMBLY OF THE LORD? For Aaron to be kohen gadol (high priest) and Moses, who taught Aaron, to be above him.
HE FELL UPON HIS FACE. Willingly. Other say, like prophets when they receive a prophecy.
WHO ARE HIS. Which is the chosen tribe. This was Moses’ answer to Dathan and Abiram and to the leaders of the congregation who were first-born.
AND WHO IS HOLY. In his tribe to be kohen gadol .
THIS. Test.

YE TAKE TOO MUCH UPON YOU, YE SONS OF LEVI. The meaning of our clause is found in the following words of Moses: Is it but a small thing unto you (v. 9). Scripture says, And Moses said unto Korah (v. 8), for the first statement was addressed to Korah and to all of his company. However, this one was addressed to the Levites.
IS IT BUT A SMALL THING UNTO YOU. This means is it but a small thing unto you.
BEFORE THE CONGREGATION TO MINISTER UNTO THEM. When they bring their burnt offerings and sacrifices.
AND THAT HE HATH BROUGHT THEE NEAR. And when he has brought you and your brothers near, will you seek the priesthood also?

THEREFORE. Therefore you and your whole congregation that art gathered together, rebel against the Lord. Its meaning is similar to And the rulers take counsel together, Against the Lord , and against His anointed (Ps. 2:2). They gathered in order to fight with God. When they strove against the Lord (Num. 26:9) is similar. Some say that the heh prefixed to no’adim (gathered together) is superfluous.
AND AS TO AARON, WHAT IS HE. What is his sin, what did he do?

WE WILL NOT COME UP. It is possible that the tent of meeting was on a high place in the middle of the camp. Scripture therefore says, Get you up from about (v. 24). On the other hand, one who goes to serve God or to the chosen place is said to go up.

IS IT A SMALL THING. Is it a small thing that thou hast brought us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey?Scripture reads, brought us up , because Egypt is south of the Land of Israel, and one who comes from Egypt to the land of Canaan is in truth going up.
BUT THOU MUST NEEDS MAKE THYSELF ALSO A PRINCE OVER US. You brought us out of Egypt in order to make yourself a prince over us.
MUST NEEDS MAKE THYSELF A PRINCE OVER US. You and your brother also seek additional positions of power over us.

MOREOVER THOU HAST NOT BROUGHT US UNTO A LAND FLOWING WITH MILK AND HONEY. Its meaning is: You brought us out of a good place. Now if you had brought us to a place which is as good as the place you took us out of, and if you had given us fields and vineyards such as we had in Egypt, and you sought power over us, then we would tolerate it. However, you removed us from a good place, from our fields and vineyards, and you did not bring us to a place as good as the one that you brought us out of. Why then do you seek power?

WILT THOU PUT OUT THE EYES OF THESE MEN? Its meaning is: you want to put out the eyes of these men. This alludes to those who left Egypt. It is as if Korah said, you want to put out their eyes so that they do not see. But what you did is visible to the eyes. Therefore we will not come up. It is metaphoric to say so and so’s eyes are closed and he therefore cannot see. Others say its meaning is: Do you want to darken the eyes so that they do not see? In other words, you are fooling us. We will not come up. Others say its meaning is: even if you put out our eyes we will not go up. Korah said of these men because he spoke in the manner of the unintelligent, who do not want to say anything negative about themselves. However, I believe that of these men alludes to the elders who were with Moses, for Scripture clearly states, and the elders of Israel followed him (v. 25).

AND MOSES WAS VERY WROTH. With what Korah said.I have already explained that the burnt offering and the meal offering put off the punishment of the wicked. Dathan and Abiram were important men and offered meal offerings before this event. This is the meaning of Respect not their offering and turn to me, for I have not placed a burden upon one ass of their asses.
[I HAVE NOT TAKEN ONE ASS FROM THEM.] I have not placed a burden upon one of their asses.
NEITHER HAVE I HURT ONE OF THEM. In any way.
AND MOSES SAID UNTO KORAH. Moses had already said so. Thus this means: when Moses said to Korah be before God, they took their fire-pan.
TOMORROW. This occurred on the day that Moses called to Dathan and Abiram. It is possible that he called them earlier. The latter appears correct because Scripture reads, in the morning (v. 5).
WITH MOSES AND AARON. Moses and Aaron with them.
SEPARATE YOURSELVES. For they were with them in front of the entrance to the tent of meeting.
AND THEY FELL UPON THEIR FACES. To pray.

[O GOD.] The term El (God) indicates that God has the power to destroy them in a moment. God is the God of the spirits . This explains the term El , for God can destroy them because their spirits are in His hand.

SHALL ONE MAN SIN. The reference is to Korah , who assembled all of the congregation against Moses and Aaron. There are those who say that the meaning of O God, the God of the spirits is: God has the power to investigate human souls, for He is their God. God knows that one man, namely, Korah alone, sinned. He also knows if he [Korah] caused the others to sin.I believe that Separate yourselves from among this congregation refers to Korah and his congregation. A fire went out and devoured and destroyed them in one moment.

THE DWELLING OF KORAH. I believe that Korah had a tent for his household and his wealth. This tent was far from the camp of the Levites. The tents of Dathan and Abiram were close to Korah’s tent, for only Levites camped around the tabernacle. We learn from this verse that the bearer of the banner camped close to the camp of the Levites.
AND THE ELDERS OF ISRAEL FOLLOWED HIM. I believe that the reference is to the chosen seventy elders.
AND TOUCH NOTHING OF THEIRS. For if one comes to save their money they will go down to the pit like them.
IN ALL THEIR SINS. Because of all their sins.
AND THEIR SONS. The reference is to adults.
AND THEIR LITTLE ONES. Male and female minors.

TO DO ALL THESE WORKS. To have the Levites take the place of the first-born. Note, it is a major and grievous act to the one who does not believe that God ordered the first-born to be removed from their position as kohanim and to have this status conferred only upon the family of Moses. All of this was done because of the incident of the golden calf, because and offered burnt-offerings, and brought peace-offerings (Ex. 32:6) speaks of the first-born who offered these sacrifices, for they alone were the kohanim . Also, the sons of Levi killed those who served the calf. There is a question here. Its answer is found in the Torah portion which opens with the words va-yelekh mosheh (Deut. 31:1).

BUT IF THE LORD MAKE A NEW THING. Some say that the word beri’ah (a new thing) refers to the bringing forth of something that was never in existence.I have already explained that the word beri’ah is related to the word u-vara (hack) in and hack them (Ezek. 23:47). Many cities have been split open, and those who dwelt in them have gone down to the pit. The meaning of bara is to cut.

AND THE GROUND OPEN HER MOUTH. The word u-fatzetah means and opened. Compare, yiftzeh (doth open) in doth open his mouth (Job 35:16).I have already hinted that man’s highest soul, which comes from the intermediary world, employs human language when speaking of things above her, for the body is its palace. It similarly employs human language when speaking of things below her. It does so in order that people understand her.
AND THEIR HOUSEHOLDS. This is a general term for their wives, [grown] children, and their little ones.
AND THEIR GOODS. Which all of them possessed.
SO THEY…WENT DOWN. Its meaning is: when they went down, the earth closed and they were not seen.
AND THE EARTH CLOSED UPON THEM. The earth itself.
AND THEY PERISHED. For their children who were to take their place died.
AT THE CRY OF THEM. Because of their cry.

[AND FIFTY MEN.] The heh of ha-chamishim (the fifty) is to be read as if written twice. Some say that Korah was among the ones who were swallowed. They offer as proof, And the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up together with Korah (Num. 26:10). Others say that Korah was burned. They offer, with Korah, when that company died; what time the fire devoured ( Ibid .) as proof. Our sages say that Korah was burned and swallowed.I believe that only the place of Dathan and Abiram split open, for no other place is mentioned. Korah was standing with his fire-pan with Aaron and the leaders of the congregation who were offering incense. With Korah (Num. 26:10) is not connected to and swallowed them up ( Ibid .) but rather to when that company died ( Ibid .). This is the way the aforementioned verse is to be interpreted. If someone should argue and say, “Why isn’t Korah mentioned among those who were burned?” the answer is: once Scripture mentions that Korah’s company, which came to his aid, was burned, it is not necessary to mention Korah. For we know this by arguing from a minor to a major premise. Pharaoh’s chariots and his host hath He cast into the sea (Ex. 15:4) is similar. Moses does not mention in the song that Pharaoh drowned. The truth is that Pharaoh drowned, for Scripture explicitly states, But overthrew Pharaoh and his host in the Red Sea (Ps. 136:15). The verse that he fare not as Korah, and as his company (Num. 17:5) is proof that Korah was among those who were burned.
AND SCATTER THOU THE FIRE YONDER. From the altar.
FOR THEY ARE BECOME HOLY. The fire-pans are holy because they [ Korah and his company ] offered them before the Lord.
EVEN THE FIRE-PANS OF THESE MEN WHO HAVE SINNED. This explains the fire-pans (v. 2).
AND LET THEM BE MADE. The reference is to the workers.
BEATEN PLATES. Compare, And they did beat (ve-yerakke’u) the gold into thin plates (Ex. 39:3).
[FOR THEY ARE BECOME HOLY.] Because they were offered before the Lord explains for they are become holy .
THAT THEY MAY BE A SIGN. A memorial and a mark.
AND THEY BEAT THEM OUT. The beaters beat them out.
AS THE LORD SPOKE UNTO HIM BY THE HAND OF MOSES. Unto him (lo) refers to Aaron. Others say that unto him refers to Korah. However, I believe the latter to be farfetched.
ON THE MORROW. Of this day, for mochorat (morrow) is always connected to the previous day.

YE HAVE KILLED. Its meaning is, what proof is this that the tribe of Levi is the chosen one, and that Aaron was chosen to be kohen gadol ? It is possible that those who offered the fire-pans were burned because of your prayer or through your knowledge of the sciences.
WHEN THE CONGREGATION WAS ASSEMBLED. Whenever the word kehillah (assembly) is followed by the word al (on), it refers to an assembly for the sake of quarreling.
AND MOSES AND AARON CAME. Because they saw that God’s glory appeared.
GET YOU UP. For they sat in the tabernacle, which was on the high ground in the camp of the Levites, as I explained in my comments on Get you up (Num. 16:24).
AND THEY FELL UPON THEIR FACES. To pray.
TAKE THY FIRE-PAN. The reference is to a specific fire-pan.
AND LAY INCENSE THEREON. Scripture does not say, and lay “the” incense on. The intelligent will understand.

AND CARRY. The word holekh (and carry) is an imperative. It is similar to the word hoshev (make to dwell) in make thy father…to dwell (Gen. 47:6). Holekh comes from the same root as helikhi (take away) (Ex. 2:9). It means bring, the idea being it should go with you.

[AND AARON RETURNED.] And Aaron returned is connected to the section that follows, even though it is separated. I have already given you many such examples. When Aaron returned and the plague was stayed, God spoke.

RODS. Some say that the rod of Levi is not God’s rod, for God’s rod was already known. Why then write Aaron’s name on it. Others say that the rod was like the other rods. There was no difference between them. This interpretation appears correct to me.
[ONE FOR EACH FATHER’S HOUSE.] Each father’s house means each tribe. Reuben and Simeon are examples.
[FOR THERE SHALL BE ONE ROD.] Scripture tells us that there shall be one rod for the tribe of Levi because this tribe was divided into kohanim and Levites.
WHERE I MEET WITH YOU. Permanently.

I WILL MAKE TO CEASE. The word ve-hashikkoti (I will make to cease) comes from a double root. It is similar to the word ve-hatimmoti (and I will consume) in and I will consume thy filthiness from out of thee (Ezek. 22:15). It is related to the word shakhakhah (assuaged) in then was the king’s wrath assuaged (Esth. 7:10). Ve-hashikkoti (I will make to cease) means I [God] will find rest. Scripture employs human language. The rod of Levi was among the twelve. Behold, the tribe of Joseph was represented by one rod.
FOR THE HOUSE OF LEVI. The word matteh (rod of) is to be read as if written twice. Our verse is to be read as if written: the rod of Aaron, the rod of the house of Levi.

AND BORE RIPE ALMONDS. The word va-yigmol (and bore ripe) is related to the word va-yigammal (and was weaned) in And the child grew, and was weaned (Gen. 21:8). Many say that the rod came from an almond tree because the rod bore almonds. However, this is not proof. The word shekedim (almonds) has midrashically been related to the word shoked (watch) in I watch over My word to perform it (Jer. 1:12).
AND THEY LOOKED. At the handwriting of each one.

AND THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL SPOKE UNTO MOSES, SAYING. It is enough for us that we perished and were undone. Now, in addition, everyone that comes near the tabernacle will die like those who were burnt. O that we should cease dying. God then spoke to Aaron, who was the leader of the tribe of Levi, and cautioned him that the Levites not cause the Israelites to stumble. The meaning of unto Aaron (Num. 18:1) is that God communicated with Aaron through Moses. On the other hand, the clause may be taken at face value, because Aaron too was a prophet. Also, this section is proof that the rebellion took place in the desert of Sinai when the tabernacle was erected and the Levites were chosen, and the first-born were disqualified.
THE INIQUITY OF THE SANCTUARY. Which is on the inside of the veil. Its meaning is, if you do not guard the sanctuary the sin is upon you.
[AND THY FATHERS’ HOUSE.] For they carried the sanctuary.
THE INIQUITY OF YOUR PRIESTHOOD. If you do not keep the laws of the priesthood, the sin is upon you.

THE TRIBE OF THY FATHER. The reference is to Levi. Our sages say that the tribe of thy father is to be taken at face value. However, I believe that it is to be explained in keeping with my earlier interpretation. Our verse is to be read as if written, the tribe of Levi which is the tribe of your father.

THAT THEY MAY BE JOINED. The meaning of ve-yillavu is similar to ve-nispechu (and they shall join) (Is. 14:1). So too the word yillaveh (be joined) in Now this time will my husband be joined (Gen. 29:34). Look, the Levites are joined by their names.
THOU AND THY SONS WITH THEE. You and your sons, and not the Levites, shall abide before the tent of meeting.
NEITHER THEY, NOR YE. It is the way of Scripture to speak in this manner. Compare, Rule thou over us, also you, also thy son (Jud. 8:22). That means this one is like this one.
[AND THEY SHALL BE JOINED UNTO THEE.] So that you do not need the services of a stranger, namely, an Israelite.

AS A SERVICE OF GIFT. And someone who is a common man in regard to the priesthood even if he be a Levite [shall be put to death]. The burnt offering of Samuel, who was a Levi, is no argument for it was a temporary ruling, as was the case of Gideon.
FOR A CONSECRATED PORTION. I have already explained this.
OF THE MOST HOLY THINGS. For there are offerings that have a lesser degree of sacredness.
RESERVED FROM THE FIRE. Of all that they sanctify, for isheh (fire-offering) and esh (fire) mean the same, the heh of isheh being superfluous.

AND EVERY MEAL-OFFERING OF THEIRS. After they sanctify the memorial part thereof. [AND EVERY SIN-OFFERING OF THEIRS, AND EVERY GUILT-OFFERING OF THEIRS.] After they offer the designated organs of the sin offering and the guilt offering. WHICH THEY MAY RENDER
UNTO ME. The reference is to a trespass. Now the meal offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering are holier than the peace offerings.

IN A MOST HOLY PLACE SHALT THOU EAT THEREOF. Even in a most holy place, namely, in the tent of meeting shalt thou eat thereof. The tent of meeting is called a most holy place in contrast to the courtyard of the tabernacle.

THEIR GIFT. A tav is missing in the word mattanam (their gift). Mattanam is similar to the word pinnah (corner), which has the meaning of pinnatah (her corner) in Passing through the street near her corner (Prov. 7:8). On the other hand, we may be dealing with two forms.

ALL THE BEST OF THE OIL. Chelev (the best) means the most precious, the best. The reference is to the cream of the oil, for the word yitzhar (oil) means light. Its root is tzadi, heh, resh . The reference is to the fat of the olive oil.
THE FIRST-RIPE FRUITS OF ALL THAT IS IN THEIR LAND. The first of all the fruits of the ground.

[EVERY ONE THAT IS CLEAN IN THY HOUSE MAY EAT THEREOF.] This verse warns that only the clean in your house may eat of fat things and of the breast of waving and the thigh of heaving and also everything dedicated by an Israelite. The Israelite shall not eat of the latter, for it belongs to God. You [the kohen ] may eat of it.
SHALT THOU SURELY REDEEM. You shall accept the redemption money of the first-born. You shall similarly accept the redemption of the first-born of the unclean beast.
AND THEIR REDEMPTION-MONEY. This only refers to the first-born of humans.

THOU SHALT NOT REDEEM. For they are holy . You shall not accept their redemption money. Many say that the word redeem refers to the Israelites. However, the reverse is true for the word tokhelunu (thou shalt eat it) (Deut. 15:20), in which the prefix thou refers to the kohen , for Thou shalt eat it refers to the one who is obligated to eat it.

COVENANT OF SALT. A “cut covenant.” The word melach (salt) is related to the word melechah (salt) in A fruitful land turned into salt (Ps. 107:34). A salted place is said to be cut off, for nothing grows there. Compare, brimstone, and salt (Deut. 29:22).
IN RETURN. The word chelef means in return.
AND HENCEFORTH…SHALL NOT COME NIGH. This was written because of Korah’s assembly.
BUT THE LEVITES ALONE SHALL DO THE SERVICE. The word hu means himself. Others say that hu is the object. However, this is incorrect, for the service of the tent of meeting is the object.
AND THEY SHALL BEAR THEIR INIQUITY. If they do not keep the charge. Now, the tithe is their inheritance. I therefore stated: [ and among the children of Israel they shall have no inheritance ].
AND THE LORD SPOKE UNTO MOSES, SAYING. To Moses, not to Aaron, for Scripture goes on to say that the Levites are to give a tithe to Aaron from the tithe [they received].
AND AS THE FULNESS. I have already explained the meaning of the word mele’ah (fullness).
OF ALL THE BEST THEREOF. The meaning of mi-kol chelbo is, of all the best thereof. And ye shall eat the fat (chelev) of the land (Gen. 45:18) is similar.
EVEN THE HALLOWED PART THEREOF. For the tenth part thereof is the holy part.

[WHEN YE SET APART THE BEST THEREOF.] This has already been mentioned by Scripture. It is repeated in order to connect it to that which follows. Its meaning is, you are prohibited to eat of it until you set apart the best thereof, and afterwards it shall be counted [as the grain of the threshing floor] and you may eat it in every clean place.

AND YE SHALL BEAR NO SIN BY REASON OF IT. This means when you set apart the best of it you shall bear no sin through it. Furthermore, when you give the hallowed part thereof, the sacred donations of the children of Israel will be preserved. However, if you do not offer to tithe, then you will bear a sin, for you will have trespassed the commandment and profaned the holy things of the children of Israel because you ate its holy part.

THIS IS THE STATUTE. This chapter was also stated at Sinai. It was given when God commanded that they put out of the camp…whosoever is unclean by the dead (Num. 5:2). There were also people who were unclean by coming into contact with a dead body when Passover arrived (Num. 9:6). This chapter is placed here because it relates to the kohen .

A RED HEIFER, FAULTLESS. The heifer is not to be small. The Gaon says that the water of sprinkling (v. 13) is similar to honey, which is injurious to the one who has red bile but stimulates the one who has phlegm. However, there is no need for this interpretation.

AND SHE SHALL BE BROUGHT FORTH. Someone shall bring her forth. Or it means he shall have her brought forth by his command. The same applies to ve-shachat (and she shall be slain), for Eleazar did not slaughter the heifer. The word le-fanav (before his face) proves the latter.

AND THE HEIFER SHALL BE BURNT IN HIS SIGHT. Ve-saraf et ha-parah (and the heifer shall be burnt) is to be rendered, and someone shall burn the heifer. The term le’enav (in his sight) proves the latter interpretation.
CEDAR-WOOD. As in the case of a leper. I have hinted there at some secret.
THEN THE PRIEST SHALL WASH HIS CLOTHES. The kohen who burns it.

AND THE PRIEST SHALL BE UNCLEAN. The meaning of ve-tame ha-kohen (and the priest shall be unclean) is, and the kohen has already been unclean, or, as some say, the kohen shall be unclean. Until the even refers to the eating of sacred food.
A MAN THAT IS CLEAN. The reference is not to the kohen who burns the cow.
A WATER OF SPRINKLING. The meaning of niddah (sprinkling) is distance. Compare, me-naddekhem (that hate you) (Is. 66:5).
AND BE UNCLEAN UNTIL THE EVEN. Once Scripture states that the gatherer of the ashes shall wash his clothes there is no need to mention that he shall wash in water.
AND UNTO THE STRANGER THAT SOJOURNETH AMONG THEM. For the Land of Israel is holy because God’s glory is there.
EVEN ANY MAN’S DEAD BODY. Be it the body of a Jew or a non-Jew.
MAN’S…BODY. Not the body of an animal.
SHALL BE UNCLEAN. The meaning of ve-tame is, shall be unclean. It is a future form, for the vav changes the verb from a perfect to an imperfect. However, I believe that ve-tame is in the past tense.

THE SAME SHALL PURIFY HIMSELF THEREWITH. The meaning of hu yitchate vo (the same shall purify himself therewith) is, he shall remove his sin therewith. On the other hand, the word yitchate (shall purify himself) is similar to the word techatteni (purge me) in Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean (Ps. 51:9). Those who are acquainted with the secret of numbers know that the number three is like the number seven.

BECAUSE THE WATER OF SPRINKLING. Some say that that me niddah (the water of sprinkling) has the same meaning as me niddah (water of sprinkling) in it shall be purified with the water of sprinkling (Num. 31:23).
WAS NOT DASHED. The word zorak (dashed) refers to the water.
IS YET. The word od (is yet) means continuously. Compare, od (while) in While the earth remaineth (Gen. 8:22).
IN A TENT. A house has the same law as a tent. Scripture mentions a tent because Israel then lived in tents. That killeth an ox, or lamb, or goat, in the camp (Lev. 17:3) is similar.
AND EVERY THING THAT IS IN THE TENT. Garments.
COVERING CLOSE-BOUND. Two coverings.
OR A GRAVE. Of a human being.
AND FOR THE UNCLEAN THEY SHALL TAKE. See, Scripture explains how one who comes into contact with the dead shall purge himself.
A CLEAN PERSON. The reference is most probably to a kohen .

BUT THE MAN THAT SHALL BE UNCLEAN. Scripture has already mentioned, Whosoever toucheth the dead…that soul shall be cut off from Israel (v. 13). It now warns the one who touches a bone or a grave [not to defile the sanctuary].
SHALL BE UNCLEAN UNTIL EVEN. And shall not become clean until he washes.
AND WHATSOEVER THE UNCLEAN PERSON TOUCHETH SHALL BE UNCLEAN. The reference is to one who has become unclean by touching a dead body, a bone, or a grave.
SHALL BE UNCLEAN UNTIL EVEN. And washes.
IN THE FIRST MONTH. In the fortieth year. Look, the Torah does not contain any act or prophecy except in the first and the fortieth year.

[AND THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL, EVEN THE WHOLE CONGREGATION, CAME.] Scripture states this because the generation that left Egypt died in the wilderness and they who were entering Canaan came to the desert of Zin.
AND THE PEOPLE ABODE IN KADESH. For they dwelt there for many days. The latter is clearly stated in Scripture.

AND THERE WAS NO WATER FOR THE CONGREGATION. Scripture tells of two incidents. One, the death of Miriam. Two, the death of Aaron and Moses and their failure to enter the land. It begins by telling the cause of the latter.
AND THE PEOPLE STROVE. Va-yarev (strove) is a hifil .
WHEN OUR BRETHREN PERISHED. Bi-geva (when…perished) is an infinitive. It is similar to ki-shekav (when…shall sleep) in when my lord the king shall sleep with his fathers (I Kings 1:21).
OUR BRETHREN. The generation that died in the desert. They were servants of the Lord.
AND WHY HAVE YE BROUGHT. This was addressed to Moses and Aaron, for Scripture goes on to say, and they assembled themselves together against Moses and against Aaron (v. 2).
Scripture reads, And the people strove with Moses , (v. 3) because their quarrel with Moses was more intense.
HAVE YE MADE US TO COME UP. He’elitunu (have ye made us to come up) is irregular.
AND MOSES AND AARON WENT FROM THE PRESENCE OF THE ASSEMBLY. Like those who flee.
AND FELL UPON THEIR FACES. To pray. Other interpret, to prophetically inquire of God.

TAKE THE ROD. Many interpretations are offered for this incident. There is an individual opinion that Moses sinned because he said to Israel, who are the children of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: Hear now, ye rebels (v. 10). However, if this were the case why did he again say, ye have been rebellious against the Lord (Deut. 9:7). Others say that the word ve-dibbartem (and speak ye) has the meaning, and ye shall strike. It is similar to the word va-tedabber (and destroyed) in and destroyed all the seed royal (II Chron. 22:10). However, this is incorrect, for va-tedabber is related to the word dever (destruction) or to the word yadber (he subdueth) in He subdueth peoples under us (Ps. 47:4). Va-tedabber thus means, and destroyed. Indeed, it so reads in the other book. The meaning of ve-dibbartem el ha-sela (and speak ye unto the rock) thus is, and ye shall destroy the rock. Furthermore, if this is the meaning of the word, why was Moses punished? The above commentaries answer, because he hit the rock twice. However, if this is the case why was Aaron punished? Rabbi Moses Ha-Kohen the Spaniard, of blessed memory, says that some signs are performed by word of mouth, others by action and speech, as in the case of the salt which Elisha cast into the water. God commanded Moses to take the staff and strike the rock as he did in the case of the rock [at Horeb]. He added the word ve-dibbartem (and speak ye) so that the water would flow via the speech and the blow. Because Israel angered him, Moses said, are we to bring you forth water from the rock? What Moses meant was, we do not have the power to bring water out of the rock. We can only do so by the power of God. Now Moses did not make himself clear. People thought what he said was that God cannot bring water out of the rock. This is the meaning of because ye sanctified Me not in the midst of the children of Israel (Deut. 32:51). Rabbi Moses offered proof from the words of the poet who said, For they embittered his spirit, And he spoke rashly with his lip (Ps. 106:33). The sin was thus in his expressing, not by striking [the rock]. However, this too is incorrect, for Moses said, are we to bring you forth water out of this rock (v. 10). Why was Aaron punished? Furthermore, no speech is mentioned in the Torah’s description of the act of striking the rock. The proof offered by Rabbi Moses is no proof because the meaning of For they embittered his spirit is that they embittered God’s spirit. Scripture similarly writes, But they rebelled, and grieved His holy spirit (Is. 63:10). This is the meaning of They angered Him also at the waters of Meribah (Ps. 106:32). It means they angered God. Scripture similarly states, These are the waters of Meribah, where the children of Israel strove with the Lord (Num. 20:13). Scripture says, And it went ill with Moses because of them (Ps. 106:32) because they embittered God’s spirit, and He decreed that Moses not enter the land. Others say that the meaning of speak to the rock can only mean strike the rock, for a rock cannot hear. Now if this is so, why was Moses punished? Some say that Moses and Aaron were punished because they did not sing a song of praise as in Spring up, O well-sing ye unto it (Num. 21:17). They say that this is the meaning of because ye sanctified Me not (Deut. 32:51). Others say that God commanded Moses and Aaron to speak to the rock, but they did not speak to it. On the contrary, Moses struck the rock. Therefore they were both punished and they were told, ye trespassed (Deut. 32:51); ye rebelled (v. 24); ye believed not in Me (v. 12), and ye sanctified Me not (Deut. 32:52). Those who are guided by reason say that it is impossible that a messenger of God would alter God’s word. If Moses transformed God’s word, how can we believe his Torah? However, the aforementioned also spoke incorrectly, for if Moses had altered a commandment he would have been punished immediately. Look, Moses was punished with regard to something which was not an eternal commandment and not a law given to Israel. Nor did he knowingly violate God’s command. He only did so inadvertently because Israel angered him. Moses clearly said, Also the Lord was angry with me for your sakes (Deut. 1: 37) . Others say that Israel told Moses to bring water out of a different rock. They offer this rock as proof (v. 10). However, Moses was afraid to alter God’s word. Moses was punished because he did not believe that he would be able to bring forth water from the rock that Israel chose. He was therefore punished. This is the meaning of ye believed not in Me (v. 12). This interpretation is also incorrect, for Scripture states, ye rebelled against My word (v. 24). However, they did not rebel.I will reveal in hints the explanation which appears correct to me. Know, when the part knows the All, he cleaves to the All and creates signs and wonders with the help of the All. Now it is true that God told Moses and Aaron, speak ye unto the rock . They did not speak to the rock because the people were quarreling with Moses. The “part” thus remained a “part.” He struck the rock, and water did not come out of it until he struck it a second time. Moses and Aaron thus did not sanctify God’s name. They inadvertently rebelled and trespassed. It is also possible to explain that And he spoke rashly with his lips (Ps. 106:33) refers to Moses. It was unseemly for Moses to say anything before fulfilling God’s command. Moses was therefore punished. The midrashic interpretation of our ancients, of blessed memory, who said that Moses sinned because he said, Hear now, ye rebels (v. 10) is also in keeping with this interpretation. The rabbis hint at this secret.
UNTO THE ROCK. Which I pointed out to you or which is found close to the camp.

THAT IT GIVE FORTH ITS WATER. Many erred and said that the rock is to be identified with the stone [at Horeb] because Scripture reads, its water. However, they cannot think straight. The stone was in Horeb and this rock was at the border of the land of Edom, for it was in Kadesh. It is also possible to interpret its water as meaning, the water which I will place in it.
THE ROD FROM BEFORE THE LORD. The reference is to the rod of God. It was the rod which was placed before the testimony.
ARE WE TO BRING YOU FORTH WATER OUT OF THIS ROCK? Do we have the power to bring forth water out of this rock for you?
BECAUSE YE BELIEVED NOT IN ME. This alludes to the secret at which I hinted, i.e., that God’s name was not sanctified through them.
AND HE WAS SANCTIFIED IN THEM. Through Moses and Aaron. Our verse has the same meaning as Through them that are nigh unto Me I will be sanctified (Lev. 10:3).

FROM KADESH. Kadesh is the name of a place where a city is located. It is not to be identified with Kadesh-barnea, for the latter was a wilderness. Thus Scripture reads, The Lord shaketh the wilderness of Kadesh (Ps. 29:8).
THE TRAVAIL. I have already explained the meaning of the word tela’ah (travail).
EGYPTIANS DEALT ILL WITH US, AND OUR FATHERS. Who died. The meaning of our clause is that their evil lasted a very long time.

AND SENT AN ANGEL. This is to be taken literally. Scripture similarly states, And the angel of His presence saved them (Is. 63:9). Many said that the reference is to Moses for they found Then spoke Haggai the Lord’s messenger (malakh) (Haggai 1:13). However, this is not my opinion.
THROUGH FIELD OR THROUGH VINEYARD. So that they do not destroy it. We will not even drink the water of your wells.
WE WILL GO ALONG THE KING’S HIGHWAY. The major highway upon which the king travels. Or its meaning is, the road that the king, namely, the king of Edom, will command us to travel in.
WE WILL GO UP BY THE HIGHWAY. What harm will it cause you if we up by the highway? If we need water you will sell it to us. This is the meaning of mikhram (v. 19). It means the price thereof.

[THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL.] Its meaning is, the entire congregation . Because Edom went to fight against them, Scripture relates that no one was missing from the children of Israel when they came from the city of Edom to Mount Hor.
AARON SHALL BE GATHERED UNTO HIS PEOPLE. This is similar to and die in the mount (Deut. 32:50). It means that Aaron should prepare himself to die, and go up the mountain.
YE HAVE REBELLED. I have explained this.
AT THE WATERS OF MERIBAH. Le-me merivah means at the waters of Meribah. It is the name of a place. Or le-me merivah means because of the waters of Meribah.
AND STRIP…AND PUT THEM UPON. Ve-hafshet (and strip) and ve-hilbashtam (and put them upon) are hifils .
[AND AARON SHALL BE GATHERED.] Its meaning is, as soon as you strip Aaron of his garments, he shall die.
AND AARON WAS GATHERED TO HIS PEOPLE. I have explained this.
AND WHEN ALL THE CONGREGATION SAW. When they saw the event which occurred, they wept for thirty days.
[DIED.] I have already explained the meaning of the term.

AND THE CANAANITE, THE KING OF ARAD. The ancients said he is Sihon. He is called a Canaanite, for all Amorites are Canaanites. Many say that Joshua wrote this section. The king of Arad, one (Josh. 12:14) is proof of this. They also found that Scripture states that the children of Judah called the name of the place Hormah. However, they are wrong, for that place was originally called Zephath while the place spoken of in our verse was ruled by the king of Arad. In reality they are two places. There are many such instances in Scripture. According to the plain meaning of the text the king of Arad ruled over the eastern bank of the Jordan. This portion was connected to the death of Aaron, because Scripture relates what happened on Mount Hor before they [Israel] journeyed from there. And the Canaanite, the king of Arad… heard…and they journeyed from mount Hor (v. 4) is proof of this. If you want to find what the king of Arad heard, observe, it is clearly stated.
THAT ISRAEL CAME BY THE WAY OF ATHARIM. Some say that the alef of atharim is superfluous. They say that the meaning of ha-atharim is, those who spy. The alef of ezro’akha (your arm) is similar.
TO COMPASS THE LAND OF EDOM. Zalmonah and Punon, for this is explicitly stated in Scripture.
THIS LIGHT BREAD. The word ha-kelokel (this light) means the very light. The word is formed by doubling the word kal . There are many similar instances in Scripture.

AND THE LORD…SERPENTS. The word ha-serafim (fiery) is an adjective. The following is a midrashic interpretation. Scripture states, If the serpent bite before it is charmed, Then the charmer hath no advantage (Eccles. 10:11). These people sent their tongues to bite. They were repaid with snakes being sent against them.
MAKE THEE. A form of a fiery serpent out of brass , for Scripture explicitly says so.

AND SET IT UPON A POLE. So that it be on a high place and everyone will be able to see it. Many err. They say that this was an image that had the capability of receiving powers from on high. Far be it, far be it [for one to believe such a thing], for this thing was made by God’s command. We should not investigate why Moses was commanded to make the form of a snake. Should someone disagree, let him show us if there is a tree that makes bitter waters sweet. Even honey will not sweeten them. What reason was there to put a cake of figs upon a boil? It is not in the nature of figs to remove boils. The truth is that the mind of the Almighty is beyond us.

AND THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL JOURNEYED. From the land of Edom, for Scripture states, to compass the land of Edom (v. 4). Punon is on the far border of Edom. The Israelites traveled from Punon to Oboth, for Scripture says so.
AND PITCHED IN THE VALLEY OF ZERED. Zered is elsewhere referred to as Dibon-gad.
FOR ARNON IS THE BORDER OF MOAB. It was so at first.

IN THE BOOK OF THE WARS OF THE LORD. It was a separate book in which the wars of the Lord on behalf of His servants was recorded. It is possible that it originated in the days of Abraham, for many books, such as the work of Nathan and Iddo, the chronicles of the kings of Israel, and the songs of Solomon and his proverbs, were lost and are not found among us.

VAHEB IN SUPHAH. There were wars in these mentioned places in ancient times. The word Vaheb is not Hebrew. Neither is Vophsi (Num. 13:14), Vashti (Esth. 1:9), Vaizatha (Esth. 9:9), and also Vashni (I Chron. 6:13). It is possible that the vav of Vashni is a connective. I say all this because we do not find the vav to be a root letter at the beginning of a word except in the word vave (hooks) in the hooks of the pillars (Ex. 27:10). It is found only in place of a yod . Compare, valed (child) (II Sam. 6:23). The explanation of the Aramaic translation is known.
AND THE SLOPE OF THE VALLEYS. Some say that the word eshed (slope) is Aramaic. The end of the matter is: all of these are names of places.
THAT INCLINETH. The reference is to the Israelites, for they passed by Ar.

AND LEANETH UPON THE BORDER OF MOAB. This is what and they abide over against me (Num. 22:5) refers to. Israel journeyed from there to a place called be’er , for the heh of be’erah (to Beer) is in place of the word el (to). It is like the heh of mitzraymah (to Egypt) (Gen. 12 :10). This well was also the result of a miracle. I believe that it is not the well which is called Miriam’s well. On the contrary, it refers to a place that Moses commanded to be dug. The princes of Israel dug it with their staffs, and water immediately gushed forth.
SPRING UP, O WELL. This is how the song opened. Scripture does not record the entire song.
SING YE UNTO IT. The word enu (sing) is an imperative. Note, Scripture explains how it came into being.
WHICH THE NOBLES OF THE PEOPLE DELVED. Scripture repeats itself, as is its style.

WITH THE SCEPTRE. The meaning of bi-mechokek (with the sceptre) is, by the governors. Compare, My heart is toward the governors (chokeke) of Israel (Jud. 5:9). This well was in the wilderness, far from an inhabited place. From this wilderness Israel journeyed to Mattanah. From Mattanah they journeyed to Nahaliel. Note that eshed ha-nehalim (the slope of the valleys) and the wilderness which is called Beer and Mattanah and Nahaliel are all names of places. They are also referred to by a general name, viz. , Almon-diblathiam (Num. 33:46), which is found in the Torah portion Ve-Elleh Mase ( Ibid. ). On the other hand, it is also possible that these are the names of places that the Israelites passed over in another journey. The mountains of Abarim in front of Nebo (Num. 33:47) are to be identified with Bamoth and the valley that is in the field of Moab (v. 20). The following is proof of this. Scripture states that Israel journeyed from the valley to the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho (Num. 22:1). It also states that Israel journeyed from the mountains of Abarim to the plains of Moab beyond the Jordon at Jericho (Num. 33:48). It further states, So we abode in the valley over against Beth-peor (Deut. 3:29) at the time that I [Moses] pleaded [with God]. Scripture elsewhere states, Get thee up into this mountain of Abarim, unto mount Nebo (Deut. 32:49). Scripture also states, and he was buried in the valley (Deut. 34:6). The Torah there states, And Moses went up from the plains of Moab unto mount Nebo to the top of Pisgah (Deut. 34:1). The valley was thus at the top of Pisgah. Moses died there, and there was no need to move him after his death.
WHICH LOOKETH DOWN. Ve-nishkafah (which looketh down) is in the feminine. It refers to the valley.

UPON THE DESERT. The word yeshimon (desert) means a wasteland ( shemamah ). And in the waste, a howling wilderness (yeshimon) (Deut. 32:10) is the proof text. So too is They wandered in the wilderness (yeshimon) in a desert way (Ps. 107:4).
TO JAHAZ. Yahtzah means to Jahaz.
FROM THE ARNON. Which he [the king of Edom] took from Moab.

EVEN UNTO THE CHILDREN OF AMMON. Scripture records that half of the land of Ammon belonged to the children of Israel, for they took it from the Amorites who originally took it from the children of Ammon. Now Scripture tells us that God would not give the Israelites even the size of a footstep from any of the land belonging to the Ammonites and Moabites. The reference is to the land which Ammon and Moab possessed at that time. Scripture therefore had to record the words of the poets. It did so because Israel lived in Heshbon. The Torah explicitly states, And Israel dwelt in all the cities of the Amorite, in Heshbon (v. 25).
AND IN ALL THE TOWNS THEREOF. Heshbon is like a mother, and the towns are like daughters.
FOR HESHBON WAS THE CITY OF SIHON. It turned into the city of Sihon, for, as was well known, he fought against the former king of Moab.
THEY THAT SPEAK IN PARABLES. Who invent parables on their own.
[COME YE TO HESHBON.] They said this to the Amorites.
BE BUILT. Better than before.
AND ESTABLISHED. To be the city of Sihon.
FOR A FIRE IS GONE OUT OF HESHBON. This alludes to the people of Heshbon who conspired against their king.
A FLAME. The idea is repeated in accord with poetic style.
FROM THE CITY OF SIHON. From the city that today belongs to Sihon.
AR OF MOAB. Ar is the name of a place. It is in Moab. Compare, Beth-lehem Judah (Ruth 1:1).
THE HIGH PLACES. Bamot means the high places.
CHEMOSH. The name of an idol; Moab’s god.
FUGITIVES. Those who flee. Fugitives that run from the sword.

WE HAVE SHOT THEM. These are the words of Moses. The mem of va-niram (we shot at them) refers to the king of the Amorites and his troops. It has two interpretations. One, that va-niram is related to the word nir (kingship). It is to be read as if written twice. It is like even the prophecy, Oded the prophet (II Chron. 15:8). Our verse means, and their king the king of Heshbon was destroyed. Va-niram is similar to the word ha-oholi (my tent) in in the midst of my tent (Josh. 7:21), and to ha-erkekha (thy valuation) (Lev. 27:23). Va-niram avad cheshbon (we have shot at them—Heshbon is perished) means, their king, that is, the king of Heshbon, perished. Second, that va-niram is related to yereh va-yor (shoot; and he shot) (II Kings 13:17) and yariti (cast) (Gen. 31:51). It means, when we shot them Heshbon was destroyed.

AND WE HAVE LAID WASTE. Va-nashim comes from a double root. The chirik is in place of a short kamatz . Compare, va-yasev (led about) in But God led the people about (Ex. 13:18). Rabbi Moses Ha-Kohen says that the dagesh in the shin of va-nashim compensates for a missing alef . Compare, Who teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth (Job. 35:11) wherein an alef is missing in the word mallefenu (teacheth us). The word va-nashim is related to the word tesham (shall bear her guilt) in Samaria shall bear her guilt (Hos. 14:1). Some say that Heshbon was always the city of Sihon. In this case, Come ye to Heshbon (v. 27) is the line that the poets directed at the Moabites who came as captive to Heshbon. And for a fire is gone out of Heshbon is a metaphor for the army of Sihon. When the poets speak on behalf of the Moabites, they say, we thought that Heshbon will be destroyed and the entire land will be laid waste even unto Nophah. Or these are the words of Moses.
AND THEY TURNED. I have already explained its meaning.
EDREI. To Edrei. Scripture is being brief.
NONE LEFT HIM REMAINING. No one of the Israelites.
